raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

On DeepSeek-V4.1, every compressed attention layer maps its index source's local top-k indices to global KV-cache slots on its own (`compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`), although the indices and the block table are shared by every layer below the same index source. DSv4.1-Flash has 38 compressed layers reading 8 index sources, so one decode step launches the kernel 38 times for 8 distinct results — inside the target CUDA graph, ~2.2 µs of GPU time each (launch-bound, a few GB/s at decode shapes). A torch-profiler trace of bs=1 DSpark decode on 4×GB200 (TP4) shows 38× `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` per step, 84 µs of GPU timeline.

## Change

Build the mapping once per (index source, compress ratio) and let the layers below read through (+53/−45 in `vllm/`, no kernel change):

- `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata` gains `decode_global_topk_cache`, cleared alongside the existing per-step FlashInfer cache in `update_draft_decode_metadata`.
- `DeepseekV4Attention._decode_global_topk` fills that cache; the FlashMLA, mega-attention and FlashInfer SM120 decode paths call it instead of the kernel.
- The SM100 FlashInfer mixed sparse indices, already cached for SWA-only layers, now cache compressed layers under `c{ratio}a:{index source}` — the same shape the DSv4 backend uses (`swa_only` / `c128a`).
- Output-neutral by construction: consumers receive the very tensors the first layer of the step built.

Not a duplicate: #57434 does this for the ROCm backend only (`deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`, ragged form) and leaves the NVIDIA paths untouched; #49678 is the same idea for GLM-5.2 in `v1/attention/backends/mla`; #41105 (draft) fuses the mapping into the DSv4 top-k kernel and keeps the per-layer recompute. Dup checks on 2026-09-19: `topk metadata across layers`, `reuse global topk indices`, `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens`, `57434 in:body`. Orthogonal to #55744 / #55692 (kernel bounds fixes in `deepseek_v4/`).

## Test Plan

GB200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_swa.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashmla.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <same files>
```

## Test Result

- `test_flashmla_sparse.py` + `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py`: **44 passed, 8 skipped**.
- pre-commit including mypy: passed.

Microbenchmark (same GB200, FlashInfer CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, `index_topk=512`, block_size 64, medians; kernel only): one launch, and a step's 38 launches (before) vs 8 (after):

| Tokens | 1 launch (µs) | Per step, 38× → 8× (µs) |
|-------:|--------------:|--------------------------:|
| 1 | 2.18 | 68.0 → 15.6 |
| 6 (bs=1 DSpark) | 2.14 | 69.4 → 14.1 |
| 96 | 2.50 | 73.2 → 15.3 |
| 1536 | 3.87 | 116.4 → 25.1 |
| 8192 (prefill-sized) | 12.26 | 323.7 → 71.3 |

@@ -1134,6 +1136,35 @@ def _compressed_kv_cache(self) -> torch.Tensor:
         source = self._static_forward_context[self.compressed_cache_prefix]
         return source.kv_cache
 
+    def _decode_global_topk(
+        self,
+        swa_metadata: "DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata",
+        attn_metadata: "DeepseekV4FlashMLAMetadata",
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Global slot ids and lengths of the decode topk indices this layer's
+        index source published.
+
+        Every consumer of one index source maps the same local indices through
+        the same block table, so the first one per step builds them and the
+        rest read the per-step metadata cache.
+        """
+        assert self.index_source_layer_id is not None
+        assert self.topk_indices_buffer is not None
+        assert swa_metadata.is_valid_token is not None
+        key = (self.index_source_layer_id, self.compress_ratio)
+        cached = swa_metadata.decode_global_topk_cache.get(key)
+        if cached is None:
+            num_decode_tokens = swa_metadata.num_decode_tokens
+            cached = compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens(
+                self.topk_indices_buffer[:num_decode_tokens],
+                swa_metadata.token_to_req_indices,
+                attn_metadata.block_table[: swa_metadata.num_decodes],
+                attn_metadata.block_size // self.compress_ratio,
+                swa_metadata.is_valid_token[:num_decode_tokens],
+            )
+            swa_metadata.decode_global_topk_cache[key] = cached
+        return cached
+
